# Layouts data and the share .dba files

This page is for developers who change the layouts of the default sites, and for administrators and hosts who wonder
where a fresh installation's layouts come from. It answers: which files carry the `explayouts_*` rows, how the
installer loads them, and how it fits them to the content of the new installation.

## Contents

1. [Not in the packages](#not-in-the-packages)
2. [The files](#the-files)
3. [What the theme seed contains](#what-the-theme-seed-contains)
4. [How the installer loads them](#how-the-installer-loads-them)
5. [Fitting the rows to the new installation](#fitting-the-rows-to-the-new-installation)
6. [The default admin layouts](#the-default-admin-layouts)
7. [Changing the seed](#changing-the-seed)

## Not in the packages

None of the five `sevenx_multisite` packages carries a layout. A content package installs classes and objects; the
layouts, zones, blocks, collections and rules of the `explayouts` extensions live in tables of their own. The
installer creates and fills those tables in `preInstall()`, before the content packages are installed, from `.dba`
files that the extensions ship in their `share/` folders.

> **Note**
> The file `extension/expsite_data_media/data/data.sql` is deprecated and unused. The source of the layouts of a new
> installation is the `share/*.dba` files described here.

## The files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `extension/sevenx_themes_media/share/db_schema.dba` | the tables `explayouts_block`, `explayouts_block_parameter`, `explayouts_collection`, `explayouts_collection_item`, `explayouts_collection_query`, `explayouts_layout`, `explayouts_rule`, `explayouts_rule_condition`, `explayouts_rule_target`, `explayouts_zone`, `eztags`, `eztags_attribute_link`, `eztags_keyword`, `ezurl`, `ezurl_object_link`, `ezstarrating`, `ezstarrating_data`, `ezpdf_export` |
| `extension/sevenx_themes_media/share/db_data.dba` | the rows of those tables (all but `ezpdf_export`) |
| `extension/explayouts/share/db_schema.dba` | the same ten `explayouts_*` tables plus `explayouts_share`, the three `eztags*` tables, `ezurl`, `ezurl_object_link` and `exp_info_collection` |
| `extension/explayouts/share/db_data.dba` | rows for its tables |
| `extension/explayouts/share/fragments/admin_layouts_db_data.dba` | the default admin layouts, see below |
| `extension/explayouts/sql/<engine>/` | `schema.sql` for `mysql`, `pgsql`, `postgresql`, `sqlite` and `oracle`, `schema.json` for `mongodb`, and `data.sql` for `oracle` |

A `.dba` file is a PHP file with a `var_export()`ed array (`$schema` or `$data`) that `eZDbSchema::read()` loads; each
table has a `fields` list and numbered `rows`.

## What the theme seed contains

Counted in `extension/sevenx_themes_media/share/db_data.dba` as it is in 6.0.15:

| Table | Rows |
|---|---|
| `explayouts_layout` | 21, all with `status` 2 (published) |
| `explayouts_zone` | 101, of which 38 are linked to a shared layout (36 to layout 2, 2 to layout 7) |
| `explayouts_block` | 342 |
| `explayouts_block_parameter` | 3648 |
| `explayouts_collection`, `_item`, `_query` | 70, 59, 48 |
| `explayouts_rule`, `_condition`, `_target` | 20, 7, 22 |
| `eztags`, `eztags_keyword`, `eztags_attribute_link` | 31, 31, 264 |
| `ezurl`, `ezurl_object_link` | 321, 495 |
| `ezstarrating`, `ezstarrating_data` | 1, 0 |

The two shared layouts (`shared` = 1) are "Header / Footer" (id 2) and "Prefooter" (id 7). The other layouts include
"Default Layout", the "Full / ..." layouts for articles, recipes, topics and videos, the landing pages of Fit &
Healthy, "Showcase", and the "Bold Agency - ..." layouts. How shared layouts and linked zones work in the editor is on
[The layouts editor](../../layouts-editor.md).

## How the installer loads them

`preInstall()` runs `dropExtensionTables()` and then `insertDBFile( package, extension, loadData )` for each entry of
`extensionSchemas()` (see [Extensions it activates](extensions-it-activates.md#extension-tables)). For the layouts the
order is what matters:

1. **`sevenx_themes_media`, schema and data.** It comes first: "its schema and data carry the layouts, tags and ratings
   of the demo content". Its tables are created and its rows inserted.
2. `ezstarrating`, `ezgmaplocation`, `eztags`, schema only.
3. **`explayouts`, schema and data.** `insertDBFile()` leaves out every table that already exists, "with their data,
   instead of failing 'already exists'". So the ten `explayouts_*` tables, the tags and the URL tables keep the
   theme's rows, and only the tables the theme does not declare (`explayouts_share`, `exp_info_collection`) are
   created here.

Details of `insertDBFile()`:

- The extension's files are looked for in `<package path>/ezextension/<extension>` when a package of that name is in
  the package repository, else in `extension/<extension>` (`extensionBasePath()`).
- Before inserting, `dropExtensionTables()` drops every table any of these schemas declares. Because the theme's
  schema declares `ezurl` and `ezurl_object_link`, those two tables are recreated with the theme's rows as well.
- When `eZDbSchema` has no handler for the database, the engine's files in `sql/<engine>/` are used: `mysql.sql` or
  `schema.sql`, `postgresql.sql` or `schema.sql`, `sqlite.sql` or `schema.sql`, `schema.sql` on Oracle,
  `schema.json` on MongoDB (directory `mongodb`), then `data.sql` or `democontent.sql` from `sql/<engine>/` or
  `sql/common/`.
- `createMissingSchemaTables()` then creates any declared table that the schema insert left out and reports the ones
  it cannot create.

## Fitting the rows to the new installation

The seed was written against the node and object ids of the reference content. After the content is installed,
post-install step 35 (`sevenxFixPackageNodesAndExplayouts()` in `post-install-fix.php`) maps each package id to the id
the new installation gave that node or object, and classifies every reference as **mapped** (rewritten), **base**
(base data such as node 1, kept) or **missing** (content the package does not ship, removed):

| Table / column | Mapped | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| `explayouts_rule_target.target_value` (types `content_node`, `ibexa_subtree`, `subtree`, `node`) | rewritten | row deleted; a rule left without targets is disabled |
| `explayouts_collection_item.value_id` (`ez_location`, `ez_content`) | rewritten | row deleted |
| `explayouts_collection_query.parameters` (`parent_location_id`, `topic_content_id`) | rewritten | set to 0 |
| `explayouts_block_parameter` `content` | rewritten | emptied |
| `eztags_attribute_link.object_id` | rewritten | row deleted |

With the full demo content nothing is missing; with `sevenx_multisite_democontent_clean` these removals are what keep
the layouts from pointing at unrelated objects. Later steps finish the job: step 40 switches off title-block links
(`explayouts_block_parameter` `link`, `use_link`) to paths that do not resolve, and the resolver cache is cleared
(`expLayoutsResolver::clearCache()`). The `ezstarrating` row of the "Test Product" is re-keyed in step 5, with its
average restored to 4.3 because "a .dba cannot carry a fractional one".

## The default admin layouts

Step 36, `postInstallImportAdminLayouts()`, loads `extension/explayouts/share/fragments/admin_layouts_db_data.dba`:
three layouts with ids from 100001, "Admin: left, main, right" (`admin_3col`), "Admin: left, main" (`admin_2col`) and
"Admin: main only" (`admin_full`), with their zones, blocks and six rules. It does nothing when an admin layout already
exists or the fragment is missing. The `admin4l` design builds the administration pages from these layouts; see
[admin4l](../../../features/6.0/admin4l.md).

> **Note**
> The fragment's own header comment still says "Prepared fragment: NOT read by the installer". That comment predates
> step 36; the installer does read it.

## Changing the seed

- Edit the layouts on a working installation, then export the tables back into the theme's `share/db_data.dba`.
  The seed of 6.0.15 holds published layouts only (every `explayouts_layout` row has `status` 2); a draft is one
  editor's work in progress and does not belong in it.
- Never review a `.dba` change by its text diff: removing one row renumbers every row after it. Compare the files row
  by row instead.
- Test the result with a full install into a throwaway database; see
  [Testing in a sandbox](../your-own/testing-in-a-sandbox.md).
